response.query: How can we operationalize recruitment and participation strategies to mitigate the digital divide, ensure language/literacy accommodations, and monitor differential loss-to-follow-up by SES and race/ethnicity?
response.answer: To mitigate the digital divide, use multilingual outreach and digital literacy training. Monitor loss-to-follow-up by SES and race/ethnicity with targeted surveys and feedback loops. Ensure diverse recruitment through community partnerships and inclusive materials.

results.content: Students must successfully complete 20.0 units with the following requirements: ❏ a minimum of 9.0 and a maximum of 11.0 units in the honours subject as follows: ❏ WOMS 1110 ❏ WOMS 1112 ❏ WOMS 3309 or 3310 ❏ WOMS 3311 or 3312 ❏ WOMS 4411 or 4412 ❏ WOMS 4499 ❏ 5.5 units of WOMS or departmental Women-Emphasis courses, including at least 0.5 unit from each of two different departments, and at least 2.5 units taken at the 3000 level or above ❏ a second combined major specified by another program (Aging, Biology, Canadian Studies, Chemistry, Communication Studies, Cultural Studies, Economics, English, Family Science, French, History, Mathematics, Political Studies, Psychology) ❏ 1.0 unit from each core group A, B, and C listed on page 67 (exclusive of the honours subject): ❏ Core A - Sciences & Mathematics (1.0 unit) ❏ Core B - Social Sciences (1.0 unit) ❏ Core C - Humanities (1.0 unit) ❏ at least 8.0 units of the total 15.0 units overall required for the combined majors must be at the 3000 level or above ❏ at least 9.0 units of the total 20.0 units must be at the 2000 level or above ❏ obtain a minimum GPA of 3.0 and a grade of at least C- in 9.0 units of the required WOMS honours courses ❏ achieve a minimum of B- in the honours thesis ❏ obtain an overall GPA of 3.0 or better in all courses counted for the degree beyond the first 5.0 units taken ❏ Note: No more than 2.0 units from professional areas may be counted toward the degree.
